Layers

PA-3 Campaign

Paul is running as a write-in candidate for the U.S. House of Representatives in Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District. The campaign runs on Square Party terms: it's as much about the framework as the office.

Help us make our laws better!

Rather than rely on paid lobbyists and well-connected staffers and who knows who else, let's just start doing it.

It's a big job. But we can break it down into small parts and let anyone learn as much or as little as they want and still participate meaningfully.

The approach I'm trying is to map the power structures onto the people they actually affect — that's you.

In theory, we can develop proposals for new regulations or laws (as well as getting rid of ones that have no reasonable purpose). But first, the framework needs human verification. Statistics are easy to check; this won't work unless people go talk to other people in the world and report back. Surveys and other tools are coming, but for now you can see how the mapping of power to representation by constituents is coming along.

GitHub is open for updates and corrections to existing information. Discussions about future areas can be started with an issue. More user-friendly options for interaction will be added after the development phase.

Two tracks

The campaign runs on two parallel tracks that share infrastructure but serve different purposes.

The voter track is for people who want to pledge a write-in vote. One question, one email, one click.

Pledge a write-in vote for Paul

This form is being built. Once the Tally form exists, swap the form ID in src/_data/site.js and it'll appear here.

For the mechanics of writing in (and a few options other than "Paul Plonski"), see How to vote →.

The content track is the deeper work — applying a People's Assembly framework to PA-3 specifically, mapping where formal representation falls short of lived experience, and inviting contributors to push back on the analysis. That's the empower project.

The two tracks feed each other but don't block each other. Pledging a vote doesn't require reading the analysis. Reading the analysis doesn't require pledging a vote.

Why a write-in

Pennsylvania's ballot-access rules for new parties and independents are demanding. The write-in path keeps the focus on the actual work rather than on the procedural challenge of getting on a ballot. It's also an honest reflection of where this stands: a project that reaches voters through write-in support is one that has earned that support on its substance, not on its access.

The closest precedent is Roosevelt's 1912 Bull Moose run, the most successful third-party presidential campaign in U.S. history, which still lost. A write-in House campaign in PA-3 isn't trying to be the exception that wins. It's trying to change the conversation about what representation could look like, and to use the cycle to put the framework in front of people who might pick it up after.
